newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian refineries in Assam, Bihar to reopen Tues.
newsitem.headline: Indian refineries in Assam, Bihar to reopen Tues.

text.p: Two Indian oil refineries which were closed last week after a pipeline burst will start functioning on Tuesday, an oil company official said on Monday.
"The refineries will start functioning from Tuesday onwards," M. Bhandari, chief engineer in charge of pipelines at state-run Oil India Ltd (OIL), told Reuters.

The refineries, at Bongaigaon in the northeastern state of Assam and Barauni in the neighbouring state of Bihar, were shut down after crude oil spurting from the burst pipeline caught fire and burned for seven hours last Thursday.
"Hopefully by today evening itself we are going to start pumping by the temporary pipeline," Bhandari said.
The pipeline that burst at Hajo, 30 kms (19 miles) west of Assam's capital Guwahati, belongs to OIL and supplies crude oil to refineries in Guwahati, Bongaigaon and Barauni.
Bongaigaon Refineries and Petrochemical Ltd has an annual capacity of 2.7 million tonnes, but it currently processes about 1.6 million tonnes, officials said on Friday.
Barauni refinery is owned by Indian Oil Corp, the country's largest oil refiner. It has an annual processing capacity of 3.3 million tonnes.
Supply to the Guwahati refinery, upstream of the break, was not affected.
The crude oil pipeline starts in Dhuliajan in upper Assam and terminates at Barauni in Bihar.
OIL's Bhandari said last Thursday that reports of two explosions before the fire led him to believe that separatist militants had planted bombs that ruptured the pipeline and ignited the fire.
Several militant groups are fighting either for a separate homeland or independence in the remote northeastern state of Assam.
